title: schema-shortform-for-tool-parameters-and-guided-recovery-protocol
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Goal: introduce a compact, human-friendly JSON "lite" schema for function/tool parameters that is easy to author in prompts, easy to validate at runtime, and provides deterministic, localized error messages and guided repair hints for callers. This ticket proposes the shape, runtime validation rules, telemetry hooks, and an error-code taxonomy intended for rollout across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Background: Current full JSON Schema usage is expressive but noisy for authored tool specs embedded in prompts and model manifests. Teams frequently request: 1) shorter authoring surface, 2) predictable coercion semantics, 3) concise machine-readable error codes for telemetry, and 4) end-user repair hints for common mistakes. The proposed approach balances expressivity and simplicity.

Design summary: Use a JSON-LD-like compact object named "json_lite_contract" that supports: 
- primitive types (string, integer, number, boolean, enum)
- shape descriptors for objects with required/optional properties
- array element shorthand with bounded length
- semantic annotations: format (email, uri, iso-date), redact (boolean), stable_key (string)
- brevity features: default "type": "string" if omitted for leaf props, and terse enum shorthand as ["a","b"]

Example contract (author-facing):
{
  "method": "create_ticket",
  "params_contract": {
    "title": {"type": "string", "min_length": 5, "max_length": 140},
    "priority": {"enum": ["P0","P1","P2","P3"], "default": "P2"},
    "reporter": {"type": "object", "props": {"name": "string", "email": {"type": "string", "format": "email"}}, "required": ["name"]},
    "tags": {"type": "array", "items": "string", "max_items": 10},
    "metadata": {"type": "object", "props": {"ci_id": {"type": "string", "redact": true}}}
  }
}

Runtime validation rules:
- Strict mode (default in hosted): reject requests that violate required/enum/type constraints and return structured error code(s).
- Lenient mode (console config for Dedicated/Private): attempt well-defined coercions (number coercion from numeric string, boolean from "true"/"false"), trimming strings, and array splitting on commas for short lists. Coercions are recorded in telemetry.
- Always validate nested objects according to props; unknown properties are dropped unless contract sets "allow_extra": true.

Error taxonomy (top-level families, mapped to observability):
- ERR_SCHEMA_MISSING_REQUIRED: missing required property; include path and suggestion for minimal value.
- ERR_SCHEMA_TYPE_MISMATCH: type mismatch that cannot be coerced in lenient mode; include expected type and sample valid value.
- ERR_SCHEMA_ENUM_INVALID: value not in enum; include allowed values.
- ERR_SCHEMA_FORMAT_INVALID: format validation failed (email/uri/date).
- ERR_SCHEMA_TOO_LONG / ERR_SCHEMA_TOO_SHORT: length constraints violated.
- ERR_SCHEMA_ARRAY_BOUNDS: too many/few items.
- ERR_SCHEMA_FORBIDDEN_PROPERTY: property explicitly disallowed.
- ERR_SCHEMA_COERCED: informational-only code emitted when coercion applied.

Error response shape (machine + user friendly):
{
  "ok": false,
  "errors": [
    {"code": "ERR_SCHEMA_MISSING_REQUIRED", "path": "params.reporter.email", "message": "reporter.email is required", "hint": "Add a reporter email like 'alex@company.com'"}
  ],
  "unprocessed_input": "..."
}

Localization and guided repair hints:
- Hints are short, plain-language templates stored in contract metadata with placeholders. At runtime we render them in the caller's locale when available. Contracts may include a small "repair_hints" map keyed by error code.
- Example: "ERR_SCHEMA_FORMAT_INVALID" -> "Make sure {path} is a valid email (like hello@acme.com)."

Telemetry and metrics:
- Emit per-request validation metric with codes, coercions_applied boolean, and latency.
- Count unique error paths to build tooling that suggests contract fixes.
- Attach anonymized sample invalid payloads (redact fields flagged with "redact": true).

Compatibility and rollout:
- Phase 1 (opt-in): Add support for json_lite_contract in the manifest schema and server-side validator. Default behavior: strict mode for hosted.
- Phase 2: Add lenient mode toggle in Dedicated/Private config and SDK helpers to coerce client-side.
- Phase 3: Migrate common internal tool contracts and add backward-compatibility adaptors that accept legacy full-JSON-Schema manifests and convert them to json_lite_contract for runtime validation.

Open design trade-offs / questions: 
1) How much coercion to permit in lenient mode? Proposed: only safe, idempotent coercions (string->number, string->boolean, array split), and never coerce complex object shapes.
2) Should error codes be stable across releases? Proposed: yes — maintain compatibility guarantees and only add new codes (never change meaning).
3) Do we allow arbitrary regex constraints? Proposed: limited support with server-side cost limits and a warning label in the contract.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Spec doc merged in docs repo with examples and migration guide.
- Server-side validator implemented behind a feature flag with tests for strict/lenient modes.
- SDK helper with client-side coercion implemented for JS/Go.
- Error codes published and mapped to console alerts; telemetry pipeline includes a validation metric.
